{"items": ["[passage_read_so_far]
- Utterson comes home in low spirits and studies Jekyll's will in his business room.（Mr. Utterson）
- The will leaves all Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde, and Hyde inherits if Jekyll vanishes.（Mr. Utterson、Dr. Jekyll、the man in the middle）
- Utterson calls the will madness and now fears it is disgrace.（Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson goes to Cavendish Square to consult his friend Dr. Lanyon.（Mr. Utterson、Dr. Lanyon）
- Lanyon welcomes Utterson warmly as an old school and college friend.（Mr. Utterson、Dr. Lanyon）
- Utterson asks whether he and Lanyon are Jekyll's two oldest friends.（Mr. Utterson、Dr. Lanyon、Dr. Jekyll）
- Lanyon says Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago.（Dr. Lanyon、Dr. Jekyll）
- Utterson asks Lanyon about Hyde, and Lanyon has never heard of him.（Mr. Utterson、Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Utterson lies awake all night, haunted by Enfield's tale and the faceless figure.（Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson resolves to hunt for Hyde, thinking 'If he be Mr. Hyde, I shall be Mr. Seek.'（Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson keeps watch by the by-street door at all hours until his patience is rewarded.（Mr. Utterson）
- A small plainly dressed man approaches the door with a key, and Utterson accosts him as Mr. Hyde.（Mr. Utterson、the man in the middle）
- Utterson accosts Hyde and asks to be admitted to see Jekyll.（Mr. Utterson、the man in the middle）
- Hyde tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll is from home.（the man in the middle）
- Utterson asks to see Hyde's face and studies it.（Mr. Utterson、the man in the middle）
- Hyde gives Utterson his address in Soho.（the man in the middle）
- Hyde angrily accuses Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description.（Mr. Utterson、the man in the middle）
- Hyde snarls, unlocks the door, and disappears into the house.（the man in the middle）
- Utterson walks away deeply disturbed by Hyde's appearance.（Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson arrives at Jekyll's house and is admitted by Poole.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll has gone out.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole confirms Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole says all servants have orders to obey Hyde.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole says Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.（Mr. Utterson）

Utterson returns home troubled and studies Jekyll’s will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde if Jekyll vanishes. He calls it madness and fears disgrace. At Cavendish Square, Lanyon says Jekyll grew too fanciful years ago and has never heard of Hyde. Unable to sleep, Utterson resolves to hunt Hyde. Keeping watch by the by-street door, he accosts a small man with a key, who admits Jekyll is out, gives his Soho address, then snarls and disappears inside. At Jekyll’s house, Poole confirms Hyde has a key, comes by the dissecting room, and all servants must obey him.
